`interface IUIBridge`<br/>
**Extends:** [`IBridge`](/reference/bridges/ibridge/)<br/>
**Known subtypes:** [`UIBridge`](/reference/backends/uibridge/)<br/>
**Package:** `dev.joid.lib.bridge.ui` · **Module:** `core` · **Source:** [IUIBridge.java](https://github.com/Zeldown/JOID/blob/main/core/src/main/java/dev/joid/lib/bridge/ui/IUIBridge.java)

The contract of a UI bridge, the place where JOID opens, holds and closes the UIs of one surface.

## Description

[`JOID.open`](/reference/ui/joid/#JOID-method-open) asks [`UIBridgeRegistry.get`](/reference/backends/uibridgeregistry/#UIBridgeRegistry-method-get) for a bridge and opens the UI there; the UI stays in that bridge until it closes.
A bridge registered in `BridgeHandler.UI` extends [`UIBridge`](/reference/backends/uibridge/), which implements this interface.
This bridge takes the panels of the application only, so `JOID.open` sends every other UI to the bridges below it:

```java file="com/example/running/PanelUIBridge.java"
```

## Method details

<a id="IUIBridge-method-canHandle"></a>

### canHandle

`boolean canHandle(UI ui)` <span class="joid-qualifier">default</span>

If `true`, the bridge accepts to open the UI; it asks `canHandle(Class)` with the class of the UI by default.

`boolean canHandle(Class<? extends UI> clazz)` <span class="joid-qualifier">abstract</span>

If `true`, the bridge accepts the UIs of that class; it answers from the class alone, so that lookups without an instance give the same answer.

<a id="IUIBridge-method-getInterfaceScale"></a>

### getInterfaceScale

`double getInterfaceScale(UI ui)` <span class="joid-qualifier">default</span>

Returns a factor that JOID applies on top of the canvas scaling of the UI, read every frame; `1D` by default.
See [interface scale](/use/learn/describing-the-ui/design-canvas/).

<a id="IUIBridge-method-forceOpen"></a>

### forceOpen

`void forceOpen(UI ui)` <span class="joid-qualifier">default</span>

Closes every UI of the bridge with `closeAll()`, then opens the UI.

<a id="IUIBridge-method-replace"></a>

### replace

`void replace(UI ui, UI replacement)` <span class="joid-qualifier">default</span>

Disposes the first UI (its `onClose` listeners and the `onDetach` listeners of its nodes run, its stores and remembered fields are saved), removes it and adds the second, without transition and without `beforeClose`.

<a id="IUIBridge-method-closeAll"></a>

### closeAll

`void closeAll()` <span class="joid-qualifier">default</span>

Disposes and removes every UI of the bridge: their `onClose` listeners (never `beforeClose`) and the `onDetach` listeners of their nodes run, and their stores and remembered fields are saved.
Call it after your loop: [Close the UIs before the program ends](/use/learn/running/backends/#close-the-uis-before-the-program-ends).

<a id="IUIBridge-method-open"></a>

### open

`void open(UI ui)` <span class="joid-qualifier">abstract</span>

JOID calls it on the render thread from `JOID.open(ui)`, on the bridge chosen for the UI.
It decides what the UI replaces, then adds it.

<a id="IUIBridge-method-close"></a>

### close

`void close(UI ui)` <span class="joid-qualifier">abstract</span>

JOID calls it on the render thread from `JOID.close(ui)` once the close listeners accepted, from `JOID.forceClose(ui)`, and when Escape closes a UI.
It removes the UI from the bridge.

<a id="IUIBridge-method-add"></a>

### add

`void add(UI ui)` <span class="joid-qualifier">abstract</span>

Adds the UI to the bridge without closing anything.

<a id="IUIBridge-method-remove"></a>

### remove

`void remove(UI ui)` <span class="joid-qualifier">abstract</span>

Removes the UI from the bridge, without any close listener.

<a id="IUIBridge-method-isOpen"></a>

### isOpen

`boolean isOpen(UI ui)` <span class="joid-qualifier">abstract</span>

If `true`, the bridge holds the UI.

<a id="IUIBridge-method-isOnTop"></a>

### isOnTop

`boolean isOnTop(UI ui)` <span class="joid-qualifier">abstract</span>

If `true`, the UI is the first of its kind to receive the input: screens and popups on one side, overlays on the other.

<a id="IUIBridge-method-getUiList"></a>

### getUiList

`List<UI> getUiList()` <span class="joid-qualifier">abstract</span>

Returns the UIs that the bridge holds, sorted by `zindex`, then by opening order.

<a id="IUIBridge-method-drawHover"></a>

### drawHover

`void drawHover(UI ui, Object content, double mouseX, double mouseY)` <span class="joid-qualifier">abstract</span>

JOID calls it while the pointer rests on a node that has a text tooltip, with the content and the pointer position in design pixels of the UI.
It draws the tooltip.
